title: Proverbs, Chapter 26 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Proverbs 26 on folios 418v, 419r of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Proverbs chapter 26 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 418v, 419r.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>כַּשֶּׁ֤לֶג ׀ בַּקַּ֗יִץ וְכַמָּטָ֥ר בַּקָּצִ֑יר כֵּ֤ן לֹא־נָאוֶ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל כָּבֽוֹד׃ <sup>2</sup>כַּצִּפּ֣וֹר לָ֭נוּד כַּדְּר֣וֹר לָע֑וּף כֵּ֥ן קִֽלְלַ֥ת חִ֝נָּ֗ם לא [ל֣וֹ] תָבֹֽא׃ <sup>3</sup>שׁ֣וֹט לַ֭סּוּס מֶ֣תֶג לַחֲמ֑וֹר וְ֝שֵׁ֗בֶט לְגֵ֣ו כְּסִילִֽים׃ <sup>4</sup>אַל־תַּ֣עַן כְּ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּֽן־תִּשְׁוֶה־לּ֥וֹ גַם־אָֽתָּה׃ <sup>5</sup>עֲנֵ֣ה כְ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּן־יִהְיֶ֖ה חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָֽיו׃ <sup>6</sup>מְקַצֶּ֣ה רַ֭גְלַיִם חָמָ֣ס שֹׁתֶ֑ה שֹׁלֵ֖חַ דְּבָרִ֣ים בְּיַד־כְּסִֽיל׃ <sup>7</sup>דַּלְי֣וּ שֹׁ֭קַיִם מִפִּסֵּ֑חַ וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים׃ <sup>8</sup>כִּצְר֣וֹר אֶ֭בֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָ֑ה כֵּן־נוֹתֵ֖ן לִכְסִ֣יל כָּבֽוֹד׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool. <sup>2</sup>As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come. <sup>3</sup>A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back. <sup>4</sup>Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him. <sup>5</sup>Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit. <sup>6</sup>He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, and drinketh damage. <sup>7</sup>The legs of the lame are not equal: so is a parable in the mouth of fools. <sup>8</sup>As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so is he that giveth honour to a fool.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>ח֭וֹחַ עָלָ֣ה בְיַד־שִׁכּ֑וֹר וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים׃ <sup>10</sup>רַ֥ב מְחֽוֹלֵֽל־כֹּ֑ל וְשֹׂכֵ֥ר כְּ֝סִ֗יל וְשֹׂכֵ֥ר עֹבְרִֽים׃ <sup>11</sup>כְּ֭כֶלֶב שָׁ֣ב עַל־קֵא֑וֹ כְּ֝סִ֗יל שׁוֹנֶ֥ה בְאִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃ <sup>12</sup>רָאִ֗יתָ אִ֭ישׁ חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָ֑יו תִּקְוָ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃ <sup>13</sup>אָמַ֣ר עָ֭צֵל שַׁ֣חַל בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ אֲ֝רִ֗י בֵּ֣ין הָרְחֹבֽוֹת׃ <sup>14</sup>הַ֭דֶּלֶת תִּסּ֣וֹב עַל־צִירָ֑הּ וְ֝עָצֵ֗ל עַל־מִטָּתֽוֹ׃ <sup>15</sup>טָ֘מַ֤ן עָצֵ֣ל יָ֭דוֹ בַּצַּלָּ֑חַת נִ֝לְאָ֗ה לַֽהֲשִׁיבָ֥הּ אֶל־פִּֽיו׃ <sup>16</sup>חָכָ֣ם עָצֵ֣ל בְּעֵינָ֑יו מִ֝שִּׁבְעָ֗ה מְשִׁ֣יבֵי טָֽעַם׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools. <sup>10</sup>The great God that formed all things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors. <sup>11</sup>As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly. <sup>12</sup>Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him. <sup>13</sup>The slothful man saith, There is a lion in the way; a lion is in the streets. <sup>14</sup>As the door turneth upon his hinges, so doth the slothful upon his bed. <sup>15</sup>The slothful hideth his hand in his bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth. <sup>16</sup>The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>מַחֲזִ֥יק בְּאָזְנֵי־כָ֑לֶב עֹבֵ֥ר מִ֝תְעַבֵּ֗ר עַל־רִ֥יב לֹּֽא־לֽוֹ׃ <sup>18</sup>כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ הַיֹּרֶ֥ה זִקִּ֗ים חִצִּ֥ים וָמָֽוֶת׃ <sup>19</sup>כֵּֽן־אִ֭ישׁ רִמָּ֣ה אֶת־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְ֝אָמַ֗ר הֲ‍ֽלֹא־מְשַׂחֵ֥ק אָֽנִי׃ <sup>20</sup>בְּאֶ֣פֶס עֵ֭צִים תִּכְבֶּה־אֵ֑שׁ וּבְאֵ֥ין נִ֝רְגָּ֗ן יִשְׁתֹּ֥ק מָדֽוֹן׃ <sup>21</sup>פֶּחָ֣ם לְ֭גֶחָלִים וְעֵצִ֣ים לְאֵ֑שׁ וְאִ֥ישׁ מדונים [מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים] לְחַרְחַר־רִֽיב׃ פ <sup>22</sup>דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃ <sup>23</sup>כֶּ֣סֶף סִ֭יגִים מְצֻפֶּ֣ה עַל־חָ֑רֶשׂ שְׂפָתַ֖יִם דֹּלְקִ֣ים וְלֶב־רָֽע׃ <sup>24</sup>בשפתו [בִּ֭שְׂפָתָיו] יִנָּכֵ֣ר שׂוֹנֵ֑א וּ֝בְקִרְבּ֗וֹ יָשִׁ֥ית מִרְמָֽה׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears. <sup>18</sup>As a mad man who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death, <sup>19</sup>So is the man that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport? <sup>20</sup>Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth. <sup>21</sup>As coals are to burning coals, and wood to fire; so is a contentious man to kindle strife. <sup>22</sup>The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly. <sup>23</sup>Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross. <sup>24</sup>He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>כִּֽי־יְחַנֵּ֣ן ק֭וֹלוֹ אַל־תַּֽאֲמֶן־בּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י שֶׁ֖בַע תּוֹעֵב֣וֹת בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃ <sup>26</sup>תִּכַּסֶּ֣ה שִׂ֭נְאָה בְּמַשָּׁא֑וֹן תִּגָּלֶ֖ה רָעָת֣וֹ בְקָהָֽל׃ <sup>27</sup>כֹּֽרֶה־שַּׁ֭חַת בָּ֣הּ יִפֹּ֑ל וְגֹ֥לֵ֥ל אֶ֝בֶן אֵלָ֥יו תָּשֽׁוּב׃ <sup>28</sup>לְֽשׁוֹן־שֶׁ֭קֶר יִשְׂנָ֣א דַכָּ֑יו וּפֶ֥ה חָ֝לָ֗ק יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה מִדְחֶֽה׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart. <sup>26</sup>Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation. <sup>27</sup>Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him. <sup>28</sup>A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
